variants.text: The passage is closed. Not frozen — closed, and the seam is dry. You would have to know which nights it opens, and somebody spent forty years finding that out.
It is shut, and the cold coming off the seam has nothing to do with the weather. Whoever kept the making-nights kept them for a reason.
No handhold, no hinge, and no frost on it. Whatever opens this opens on a schedule, and the schedule is written down somewhere in the Landing.
The seam runs floor to roof and does not admit a blade. You are not going to force a thing that has been opening and shutting on its own for nine hundred years.
